text:
maya: quick sync — thinking through a long-lived approach to ship lots of small refactors safely. proposing we call it 'debt-tiling' :tiled_map: — break the monolith surface into small tiles, migrate a tile at a time with a safety net and clear rollback.

alex: short + curious — how is this different from our usual slice-by-slice plan?

maya: main differences: 1) each tile has a compiled runbook (deploy + rollback + perf guardrails) 2) tiles are sized by both code churn and runtime cost impact (not just feature surface) 3) we mandate an isolation shim for each tile so can toggle traffic at the router layer quickly.

sam: examples? give me a concrete tile we can try as guinea pig.

maya: enrichment/normalization for tenant routing. small CPU-heavy path we can isolate. plan: extract a thin adapter, add a prefix cache in runtime, and route 10% traffic for 48h. if error-rate or p99 latency regress, rollback to router toggle.

irfan: sounds good. how do we measure cost impact automatically?

maya: metric bundle per tile: token-cost-estimate, cpu-seconds, p50/p95/p99 latency, error-rate, failure-cases. arch-bot will surface deltas after each rollout window.

rita: architecture concern — what about cross-tile state? enrichment reads session metadata and writes to the global kv. we need a pattern for transactional boundaries.

alex: for that tile we can adopt eventual consistency + compensator approach. make the thin adapter write to a per-tenant queue, consumer lives in the new tile for correctness-critical flows for a transition period. config, not code hacks.

maya: exactly. minimal lateral integration: queues + sideband replay for a bounded window. runtime config controls who uses sideband vs old path.

sam: do we need a new API gate for tiles? won't explode the gateway surface area?

maya: keep a single gateway contract. router uses tile flags to pick backend. gateway API unchanged. tiles expose an internal shim HTTP endpoint not public.

alex: ops questions — can we automate the rollback toggle? I want no manual steps for fast mitigation.

maya: yes. rollout plan template (example):
```
rollout: tile/enrichment-tenant-routing
phases:
  - name: canary
    traffic: 0.05
    duration: 2h
    checks: [p99_latency < baseline + 30ms, error_rate < 0.2%]
  - name: ramp
    traffic: 0.5
    duration: 24h
    checks: [cost_delta < 10%, p99_latency < baseline + 50ms]
  - name: full
    traffic: 1.0
    duration: 48h
    checks: [steady_state]
on_failure: auto-rollback
monitoring: [tile.metrics.bundle, tracing.sample:0.1]
```

rita: that's helpful. one more: how do we prioritize tiles? we have lots of tech debt.

maya: prioritize by three factors: 1) unit-cost reduction potential 2) customer-visible latency reductions 3) churn risk (how often we touch the code). produce a score and target top 8 tiles for quarter.

irfan: technical guardrails we need in codebase to make tiles low friction?

maya: small list: clear adapter interfaces, no lateral DB schema changes without a feature flag, each tile must have its own infra module (k8s, metrics, runbook), and a test harness that replays production traces locally.

sam: can we reuse the eval harness for quality regression detection during ramp?

maya: yes — run a lightweight eval set on sampled outputs for the tile when traffic >= 50%. arch-bot will post a pass/fail summary to the thread.

alex: ownership model? who signs off each tile?

maya: owning team implements; design review by platform + runtime for safety; product weighs customer risk if behavior change; infra approves infra cost impact. signoff checklist in the runbook.

rita: risk note — hitting external vendor rate limits during ramp. include vendor quota guard in checks.

maya: added. also mandate a contingency budget for burst during ramp in dedicated pools.

arch-bot: reminder: create a repo under infra/tiling-templates with the rollout template and runbook checklist.

sam: next steps?

maya: 1) pick guinea pig tile (enrichment) — sam to lead 2) infra to create template repo — irfan 3) platform to wire router toggle API — alex 4) set measurement dashboard — rita 5) schedule a 30m walkthrough on Monday.

sam: ok taking point. will post a rough milestone doc by EOD.

irfan: creating repo now, will ping when done.

alex: I'll sketch the router toggle and provide an API doc draft.

rita: will add metrics and vendor quota checks to the dashboard.

maya: thanks team. aim for a safe, small landing to validate the pattern. if it goes well we can expand tiling next quarter and incorporate into tech debt roadmap. :rocket:
